title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan flags off ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally 2026’ dedicated to National Song Vande Mataram, today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
subtitle: Union Ministers and Members of Parliament join the patriotic bike rally at Delhi
body_text:
A grand Tiranga Bike Rally 2026 was flagged off from Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today as part of the ongoing Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 , dedicated to the National Song Vande Mataram . Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, flagged off the rally in the presence of Union Cabinet Ministers including Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Union Minister of Minority Affairs; Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal and Mines; Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment; Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and Union Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Union Minister of Panchayati Raj and Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Smt. Nimuben Bambhaniya; Shri Rao Inderjit Singh, Union Minister of state for Culture and Union Minister of state (Independent Charge) of Statistics, Programme Implementation and Planning; Shri V. Somanna, Union Minister of State in the Ministry of Railways; and Union Ministers of State for Home Affairs, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar and Shri Nityanand Rai and several Members of Parliament.
While addressing the gathering Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan expressed deep emotion on the historic occasion of commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram. He stated that these two immortal words had awakened a burning spirit of patriotism in the hearts and minds of Indians during the struggle to free the Motherland from British colonial rule. He observed that no other expression had captured the awakening of a nation with such power and resonance. Recalling that Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay had penned these immortal words, he said that they gave voice to the very soul of the nation.
Vice-President further highlighted that while people had once marched for the independence of the nation, India was now witnessing a confident and resurgent Bharat marching towards the mission set by the Prime Minister for the Viksit Bharat by 2047. He urged everyone to carry this spirit forward by actively promoting the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign in their respective constituencies, states, streets and homes. He concluded by emphasising that as the wheels began to turn, the journey should not end with the rally, and that the spirit of Vande Mataram should remain alive beyond the celebration.
Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, in his welcome address stated that the gathering was not merely for a bike rally, but was an expression of respect and support for the Tiranga, the symbol of India’s independence and an emblem that binds the nation together in one thread. He recalled that nearly five years ago, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had set before the nation the goal of making India a developed nation by 2047. He further noted that even before the beginning of the Amrit Kaal of independence, the Prime Minister had envisioned such Tiranga yatras across the country.
The rally also witnessed enthusiastic participation from over 350 CAPF bikers which included CRPF, BSF, Assam Riffles among other. Over 50 Special biker groups and women bikers also participated in the rally.
As part of the ongoing Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 campaign, dedicated to the spirit of national song Vande Mataram, citizens are encouraged to hoist the National Flag at their homes and workplaces between 9 and 17 August and actively participate in this nationwide celebration of patriotism and national unity.
***
M Annadurai

enrichment.summary: On 12 August 2026, Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan flagged off the 'Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally 2026' from Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, as part of the ongoing Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 campaign dedicated to 150 years of the National Song Vande Mataram. Several Union Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Members of Parliament joined the rally, which also saw participation from over 350 CAPF bikers (including CRPF, BSF, Assam Rifles) and more than 50 special and women biker groups. The Vice-President urged citizens to keep the patriotic spirit alive beyond the rally by actively promoting the Tiranga campaign in their homes, streets and constituencies.
enrichment.context:
The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign was launched by the Government of India in 2022 as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav to mark 75 years of independence, encouraging citizens to hoist the National Flag at their homes to foster a personal connection with the Tricolour and national identity. It has since been continued annually around Independence Day. This year's edition (2026) is specially dedicated to commemorating 150 years since Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay composed Vande Mataram, which became a rallying cry during India's freedom struggle and was later adopted as the National Song of India, distinct from the National Anthem (Jana Gana Mana). Vande Mataram holds constitutional and historical significance—it was first sung at the 1896 Indian National Congress session and played an integral role in the Swadeshi and nationalist movements, especially in Bengal.

Such symbolic mass-mobilisation events, often involving central paramilitary forces and political leadership, are typically used by the government to reinforce themes of national unity and the 'Viksit Bharat @2047' vision articulated by the Prime Minister. While this specific release documents a ceremonial flag-off event, it connects to broader constitutional and historical themes—use of national symbols, the freedom movement, and government campaigns for civic participation—that are periodically tested in the UPSC syllabus.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Song of India, Vande Mataram:
1. It was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
2. It was first sung at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress.
3. It has the same constitutional status as the National Anthem.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and first sung at the 1896 INC session. However, it is designated the National Song, a status distinct from and not equivalent to the National Anthem (Jana Gana Mana), so statement 3 is incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Har Ghar Tiranga' campaign, referenced in the 2026 bike rally event, was originally launched in which year as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign was launched in 2022 to mark 75 years of India's independence under the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav initiative.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the historical significance of the National Song 'Vande Mataram' in India's freedom struggle and its continuing role in shaping national identity today.
Examine the role of symbolic mass campaigns like 'Har Ghar Tiranga' in fostering national integration and civic participation in contemporary India.
